name: Moiré swelling band
subtitle: an armband that shows early lymphedema

effects.effect: two overlaid fine patterns make broad bands that magnify a small shift

effect: two overlaid fine patterns make broad bands that magnify a small shift
how: About one in five breast-cancer survivors gets lymphedema, a lifelong arm swelling that is easiest to reverse in its first millimetres, yet it is checked with a tape measure at clinic visits. A stretchy band carries two overlapping fine-line prints; when the arm grows even a millimetre around, the lines shift and broad stripes slide visibly along the band (moiré), so the wearer sees the change every morning.
obstacle: Telling real swelling apart from the band slipping or the arm being held differently.
why: Free daily self-checks catch lymphedema while it can still be reversed.
real: Limb-swelling wearables use capacitive sleeves, strain bands or 3D bodysuits, and moire strain indicators exist for structures, but no moire band for limb circumference was found.
